question: ________ determines the sex of fertilised eggs in a few reptiles.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Temperature**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperature** determines the sex of fertilised eggs in a few reptiles.
 
• This phenomenon is known as **temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD)**.
 
• In some reptiles, such as certain species of turtles, crocodilians, and lizards, the **ambient temperature** during a critical period of embryonic development determines whether the offspring will be male or female.
 
• This is different from the genetic sex determination seen in many other animals, where sex is determined by specific chromosomes (allosomes).
 
• For example, in many turtle species, **higher incubation temperatures** produce females, while **lower temperatures** produce males.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD)** is a type of environmental sex determination, where the environment plays a crucial role in determining the sex of the offspring.
 
• This mechanism allows for the adjustment of sex ratios in response to environmental conditions, potentially providing an evolutionary advantage.
 
• Research into TSD can help in the conservation of endangered reptile species, as understanding the temperature ranges that produce both sexes can inform breeding programs.
 
• In contrast, in genetic sex determination systems, such as those in humans, sex is determined at fertilization by the combination of sex chromosomes (XX for females and XY for males).
